notes: All Census values are 2025 dollars from the Current Population Survey Annual Social and Economic Supplement (CPS ASEC, 2026). Medians cover all households, not only households with children.

BLS values are median usual weekly earnings of full-time wage and salary workers age 25+. BLS notes that 2025 annual estimates are 11-month averages that exclude October 2025 (not collected because of the federal government shutdown), so they are not strictly comparable with other years.
Fields marked "derived": true are computed directly from the published values using the stated formula. They are not published statistics.
Fields marked "assumption": true are modeling choices for the author to confirm, not data.

householdIncomeByHouseholderEducation.description: Median household income by educational attainment of householder (householders age 25 and older)
householdIncomeByHouseholderEducation.table: Table 1. Income Summary Measures by Selected Characteristics: 2024 and 2025

householdIncomeByHouseholderEducationDet.description: Median and mean household income by detailed educational attainment of householder (householders age 25 and older). No margins of error are published in this table.
householdIncomeByHouseholderEducationDet.table: Table H-13. Median and Mean Household Income by Educational Attainment of Householders 25 Years Old and Over: 1991 to 2025

householdIncomeByResidence.description: Median household income by residence (all households). Census notes that 2025 metro/nonmetro estimates are not comparable with 2024 because of a new sample design and updated metro delineations.
householdIncomeByResidence.table: Table 1. Income Summary Measures by Selected Characteristics: 2024 and 2025

outside_principal_cities.label: Inside metro areas, outside principal cities (suburbs)

householdIncomeByHouseholdType.description: Median household income by type of household (all households). Useful for family-structure flavor text; does not isolate households with children.
householdIncomeByHouseholdType.table: Table 1. Income Summary Measures by Selected Characteristics: 2024 and 2025

workerEarningsByEducation.description: Median usual weekly earnings and unemployment rate by educational attainment, persons age 25+ (earnings are for full-time wage and salary workers). For an individual parent's pay and for job-loss event odds. Annual estimates exclude October 2025.
workerEarningsByEducation.table: Table 5.1 Unemployment rates and earnings by educational attainment, 2025
workerEarningsByEducation.unit: USD per week; unemployment rate in percent

less_than_hs.label: Less than a high school diploma

d1HouseholdIncome.description: Which published median sets familyIncome for each D1 option (before the D2 adjustment).

graduate_or_professional.note: No combined graduate/professional median is published. Master's is the most common graduate degree among householders. If the D1 scene keeps the physician parent (docs/sample-scene.md), use 'professional' (190,400) instead.

d2PlaceRatio.description: Multiplier applied to the D1 median for each D2 option: (residence median) / (all-households median).
d2PlaceRatio.assumptionNote: Applying a place ratio to an education median assumes the two effects multiply independently. These tables don't publish income by education and place together.

high_poverty_city.gap: Census CPS does not separate high-poverty neighborhoods; this uses all principal-city households.

working_class_suburb.gap: CPS does not separate working-class from affluent suburbs; both use all suburban households.

affluent_suburb.gap: CPS does not separate working-class from affluent suburbs; both use all suburban households.

small_town.gap: CPS does not separate small towns from rural areas; both use all nonmetro households.

rural.gap: CPS does not separate small towns from rural areas; both use all nonmetro households.

missing: Median household income for households with children (all values above include households without children, including retirees).
Income for high-poverty neighborhoods, and the split between working-class and affluent suburbs and between small towns and rural areas (see d2PlaceRatio gaps).
Household income by householder education and place together (the model multiplies them instead).
A single median for graduate or professional degrees combined.
Margins of error for Table H-13 values (not published).
National shares of family structures for households with children, including grandparent-led and same-sex-parent households.
Family income bracket edges (College Scorecard net-price bands) and the Head Start poverty line (HHS poverty guidelines); these belong with net-price.json and the D3 data.
